profile.campus: Aurora, Arapahoe County, Colorado (QTS Aurora-Denver 1 campus)
profile.address: 1160 N Gun Club Rd, Aurora, CO 80018
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Aurora-Denver 1 sits at 1160 N Gun Club Rd, Aurora, CO 80018 (Arapahoe County) on a 65-acre owned campus with 160+ MW of critical power capacity; no per-building sqft or cooling-redundancy figure is published.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built data center capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model it shares with peers such as Digital Realty and CyrusOne. Since Blackstone completed its roughly $10 billion take-private acquisition in August 2021, QTS has continued expanding across multiple US metros rather than slowing development, including major campus filings and expansions in Phoenix (a 750MW, 375-acre Glendale campus acquired for $255.3 million in July 2022) and Dallas-Fort Worth (its two mega-scale Irving and Fort Worth campuses), consistent with the scale of buildout QTS has also pursued in Northern Virginia, Georgia, and Ohio, tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS was originally founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas by Chad Williams, and grew through a mix of acquisitions and ground-up construction into a national wholesale/colocation platform before its 2013 IPO as a publicly traded REIT; that public period ended with the 2021 Blackstone take-private deal. QTS's current published portfolio language describes over 30 facilities across North America and Europe on its own site, while Wikipedia gives a somewhat different approximate figure of 28 locations across 16 US states plus two Netherlands sites (Eemshaven and Groningen), a discrepancy this registry notes rather than resolves in favor of either source.

reading.body:
QTS Aurora-Denver 1 occupies a 65-acre owned campus in Arapahoe County with stated critical power capacity of 160 MW or greater. The operator's own language distinguishes this as planned or build-out capacity rather than confirmed current operating capacity, so the actual power available for IT load today is not published. If the full 160 MW reaches operating status, assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, the campus could host roughly 4,000 racks. No per-building square footage, cooling redundancy, or tenant information is published.

Within Colorado, QTS Aurora-Denver 1 ranks fourth by published megawatts among facilities whose operators have stated a figure. The state has 17 mapped data center facilities total, but only three publish capacity numbers. Colorado's three published facilities total 26.35 MW, meaning this single campus would more than quintuple that total if its 160 MW capacity reaches operating status. The scale difference between published and potential capacity here reflects the gap between existing regional AI infrastructure and committed expansions.

This campus sits within a multi-region QTS footprint spanning Texas, Arizona, Ohio, New Jersey, Illinois, and Colorado. QTS itself is owned by Blackstone and was acquired as a mature operator with established facilities across North America. Whether the Aurora campus functions as regional compute capacity for AI workloads, cloud services, or other uses is not specified in the published facts.
